items.question: What is the primary value of storing a shared template in a Project knowledge base rather than in a team email or shared drive?

options.A: Claude can apply the template automatically to any output without the user needing to reference it
options.B: The template is available in the conversation context whenever needed, without requiring the user to locate and attach it each time
options.C: The template is protected from editing by team members who have Project access
options.D: Templates stored in Project knowledge are version-controlled automatically by the platform

items.question: Which question is most useful when auditing Project custom instructions for quality?

options.A: Does each instruction use precise, domain-specific vocabulary?
options.B: Can every instruction be justified by a current, recurring need that per-chat prompts should not have to handle?
options.C: Is the total instruction word count within an accepted limit?
options.D: Does each instruction reference at least one knowledge base document?

items.question: Why is a Project knowledge base particularly valuable when Claude must consistently apply a specific regulatory or legal framework?

options.A: It prevents Claude from applying any other framework, ensuring regulatory exclusivity
options.B: It provides the specific framework document as a grounding source available in every session, reducing reliance on parametric memory for regulatory specifics
options.C: Regulatory documents stored in Project knowledge are automatically updated when regulations change
options.D: It allows Claude to give legally binding advice grounded in the stored regulation

items.question: Which behavior can Project custom instructions NOT reliably produce?

options.A: Outputs in a consistent, specified prose style
options.B: Responses that always include a defined disclaimer
options.C: Factually accurate responses on topics outside the knowledge base
options.D: Outputs that follow a defined section structure

items.question: Claude consistently ignores an instruction to always respond in bullet points. What should be checked first?

options.A: Whether the Project's knowledge base documents are formatted in prose, causing Claude to mirror them
options.B: Whether another instruction in the same Project contradicts or overrides the bullet-point directive
options.C: Whether the model tier being used supports formatting instructions
options.D: Whether the platform's markdown renderer is configured to display bullet points

items.question: When should a team use separate Projects rather than one Project with a broad knowledge base?

options.A: When the team has more than a defined maximum number of documents for a single Project
options.B: When different workflows require different instructions, knowledge, or access permissions that would conflict or be inappropriate if combined
options.C: When team members are located in different offices and need regional Project settings
options.D: When the organisation wants to reduce its overall usage by distributing activity across Projects

items.question: Why does a well-curated Project knowledge base not eliminate the need for output verification?

options.A: Because knowledge base documents are stored in compressed form and may lose detail during retrieval
options.B: Because grounded responses can still be wrong if the knowledge base documents themselves are inaccurate or outdated, and Claude may also blend parametric content with retrieved content
options.C: Because Claude applies a confidence penalty to grounded responses that makes them less reliable than parametric answers
options.D: Because the platform cannot guarantee that all knowledge base documents were successfully ingested

items.question: Which instruction design provides the strongest protection against Claude producing an output that exceeds its appropriate scope in a high-stakes Project?

options.A: An instruction that specifies the model tier to use for all high-stakes queries
options.B: An instruction that explicitly names the categories of output Claude must not produce in this Project
options.C: An instruction that directs Claude to always seek clarification before producing any output
options.D: An instruction that limits the length of all responses to prevent over-production

items.question: A connector links a Project to a live team wiki. The wiki is updated frequently by multiple contributors. What ongoing governance responsibility does this create?

options.A: None — the connector handles currency automatically, eliminating manual governance
options.B: The Project owner must monitor the connected wiki for content that falls outside the Project's scope or accuracy standards
options.C: The connector must be re-authorised each time the wiki is edited to confirm the changes are intended
options.D: Contributors to the wiki must be added to the Project's user list to maintain the connection

items.question: Which TWO CKM practices directly support output verification by creating a checkable basis for responses? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Storing accurate, current reference documents in the knowledge base so responses can be checked against them
options.B: Writing custom instructions that direct Claude to cite the knowledge base document it drew on in each response
options.C: Keeping the instruction set short to reduce the number of behavioral constraints that could cause errors
options.D: Using a higher-tier model to increase response accuracy and reduce the need for external verification
options.E: Ensuring only one version of each authoritative document exists in the knowledge base

items.question: A Project's custom instructions restrict Claude to financial analysis topics. The knowledge base contains a marketing strategy document added by mistake. What is the most likely outcome?

options.A: Claude will refuse to retrieve the marketing document because the instructions have excluded that topic
options.B: The marketing document may be retrieved if a user query superficially matches its content, producing an out-of-scope response
options.C: Claude will flag the marketing document as out-of-scope and ask the Project owner to remove it
options.D: The instructions and the knowledge base are independent; instructions govern behavior while knowledge base content is always retrievable regardless

items.question: Which TWO practices together constitute a complete, sustainable knowledge base lifecycle for a team Project? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Adding all potentially useful documents at setup so the base is comprehensive from day one
options.B: Removing superseded, duplicate, and out-of-scope documents on a defined cadence and whenever source content changes
options.C: Limiting the knowledge base to documents personally authored by Project team members
options.D: Adding authoritative, in-scope documents at setup and as new reference material becomes relevant
options.E: Keeping all historical document versions in an archived state so Claude can reference past practice

items.question: What makes a Project's configuration a governance asset as well as a productivity tool?

options.A: Projects are automatically audited by the platform and generate compliance reports
options.B: The combination of access-controlled instructions, curated knowledge, and documented behavioral constraints creates an auditable, consistent AI usage record
options.C: Projects require manager approval before creation, creating a governance checkpoint
options.D: The platform retains all Project conversations indefinitely for regulatory review

items.question: What is the FIRST step in diagnosing any Claude output quality problem?

options.A: Check whether the model tier is appropriate for the task complexity
options.B: Run the prompt multiple times to determine whether the problem is consistent or intermittent
options.C: Identify the specific symptom present, because different symptoms map to different missing prompt elements
options.D: Compare the output to a few-shot example to measure the quality gap

items.question: When is escalating to a more capable model tier the correct response to an output quality problem?

options.A: After confirming that the prompt is well-formed and output still fails to meet defined requirements
options.B: After the second failed prompt iteration, to save iteration time
options.C: Whenever the task involves multi-step reasoning, as these tasks always benefit from the highest tier
options.D: When the model produces a refusal, because refusals indicate that the model tier is insufficient

items.question: Claude's output is simultaneously too long AND in the wrong format. Which troubleshooting approach is most efficient?

options.A: Fix the length first, then address the format in a separate subsequent iteration
options.B: Fix the format first, then address the length in a separate subsequent iteration
options.C: Switch to a higher model tier that can handle both dimensions simultaneously
options.D: Address both in a single revised prompt, since both are format-family elements that belong in the same section of the prompt

items.question: A workflow's prompt produces excellent output but at unacceptably high cost per call. A team suggests upgrading to a more capable model to produce shorter outputs. What is wrong with this reasoning?

options.A: Output length and model capability are independent — any tier can produce short output
options.B: Upgrading to a more capable model increases per-call cost; the correct approach is to add a length constraint or test a lower tier that meets quality at lower cost
options.C: Output length cannot be controlled by prompt instructions — it is determined by the model's capabilities
options.D: Cost reduction requires pipeline architectural changes that cannot be achieved at the prompt level

items.question: Which statement most accurately describes the correct relationship between adding context and upgrading a model tier as quality interventions?

options.A: They are interchangeable — either will improve quality on a failing task
options.B: Context addition should always follow tier escalation to confirm the escalation was justified
options.C: Context addition is tried first because it addresses the cause when information is missing; tier escalation follows only when adequate context was provided and quality still fails
options.D: Tier escalation and context addition must be applied simultaneously to measure their combined effect

items.question: A practitioner immediately switches to the highest model tier when output fails, before making any other change. Which principle does this violate?

options.A: The principle of diagnosing before escalating — the cause of failure should be identified before any intervention is applied
options.B: The principle of tier neutrality — all tiers should be tested in sequence before conclusions are drawn
options.C: The principle of cost minimisation — cost must always be minimised before quality improvements are attempted
options.D: The principle of context-first prompting — context must be added before any other prompt element is modified

items.question: When a conversation has drifted, what is the single most important factor in choosing between starting a fresh chat and restating instructions mid-thread?

options.A: The number of messages in the current thread
options.B: Whether the drift has affected format or content dimensions
options.C: Whether the current model tier supports long-context recall
options.D: Whether the prior output in the thread contains value that should inform what comes next

items.question: Output is both inconsistent across runs AND insufficiently deep. These are two distinct symptoms. Which single prompt intervention most efficiently addresses both?

options.A: Upgrade to a higher model tier, which produces more consistent and deeper output
options.B: Add explicit specificity constraints to narrow the output space and a depth instruction — specificity addresses variance while depth instruction raises the quality floor
options.C: Add more background context, since context gaps cause both inconsistency and shallowness
options.D: Add few-shot examples, since examples define both the expected output range and expected depth simultaneously

items.question: Output is well-formatted, appropriate length, and on-topic, but conclusions are logically inconsistent with each other. Which prompt element is MOST likely to fix this?

options.A: A role instruction specifying analytical expertise
options.B: A format constraint requiring numbered conclusions
options.C: A chain-of-thought instruction requiring reasoning to be shown before conclusions are stated
options.D: A context addition providing more background on the subject matter

items.question: What is the correct application of the one-variable-at-a-time principle when debugging a failing prompt chain?

options.A: Diagnose each call in the chain independently — isolate the failing call first before modifying any other part of the chain
options.B: The one-variable principle does not apply to chains because each call is already a separate prompt
options.C: In a chain, all prompts should be revised simultaneously to maintain consistency between calls
options.D: The one-variable principle only applies to single-call prompt debugging; chains follow a different debugging methodology

items.question: The same task type produces a refusal in one context and poor quality output in another context. What does this most likely reveal?

options.A: The task is inherently a poor fit for Claude regardless of context
options.B: The prompt has a content policy violation that should be escalated to technical support
options.C: The task exceeds the model's capability and requires the highest-tier model
options.D: Context is the critical variable — with appropriate professional context the task is treated as legitimate, and without it the model defaults to caution

items.question: A practitioner suspects conversation drift but is not certain. Which test definitively confirms or rules out drift?

options.A: Count the number of turns and compare to a known drift threshold
options.B: Run the same prompt in a fresh chat — if quality improves, drift is confirmed; if quality remains poor, the prompt itself is the problem
options.C: Ask Claude to summarise the current conversation and check whether the summary is accurate
options.D: Compare the current output against the first output from this thread for stylistic differences

items.question: A Project knowledge base contains two contradictory documents on the same topic. What is the correct remediation?

options.A: Delete both documents and recreate a single authoritative version from memory
options.B: Add a prompt instruction to ignore the older document when the topic arises
options.C: Remove or update the outdated document so the knowledge base contains only one authoritative version
options.D: Create a separate Project for each document version and direct users to the appropriate Project

items.question: Which symptom combination most precisely indicates that adding a worked example is the most targeted fix?

options.A: Output structure and approach are conceptually correct but inconsistent in execution — the model understands the task but lacks a concrete anchor for how to perform it
options.B: Output is generic and non-specific, suggesting that background context is missing
options.C: Output addresses a different question, suggesting that the task description is ambiguous
options.D: Output is insufficiently deep, suggesting either missing context or an insufficient model tier

items.question: When is testing a prompt across multiple model tiers a meaningful troubleshooting or optimisation step?

options.A: Before every deployment, to establish a quality baseline across all available tiers
options.B: Immediately after any output failure, before making any other change
options.C: Only when cost reduction is the stated objective of the optimisation effort
options.D: After the prompt has been refined to a well-formed state — tier comparison is meaningful only when the prompt is no longer the limiting factor

items.question: A long conversation contains highly valuable prior output AND significant drift in recent turns. The user needs to continue building on the prior work. What is the most effective strategy?

options.A: Continue in the same conversation with a comprehensive instruction restatement to re-anchor all guidelines
options.B: Start a fresh conversation, paste the valuable prior output as reference material, and restate all key instructions at the top of the new thread
options.C: Extract and save the valuable prior output externally, then continue in the same thread with an instruction restatement
options.D: Move the prior output into a new Project as knowledge base content and start a fresh conversation in that Project

items.question: Which TWO of the following represent diagnostic information that should be gathered BEFORE attempting any prompt intervention? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Whether the output failure is consistent across runs or only occurs sometimes
options.B: Whether Anthropic has recently updated the model version
options.C: Which specific symptom is present — wrong format, wrong length, wrong content, refusal, or other
options.D: Whether the user is on a paid or free account tier
options.E: Whether the prompt was written by the user or by a colleague

items.question: Which TWO of the following principles apply to BOTH single-turn prompt debugging AND multi-turn conversation management? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Always start with a fresh conversation to eliminate accumulated context before diagnosing
options.B: Change one element at a time and observe the effect before making the next change
options.C: Add few-shot examples as the first intervention for any output quality failure
options.D: Match the intervention to the symptom — different symptoms require different fixes
options.E: Upgrade the model tier as the first step for any task involving analysis or reasoning

items.question: Which TWO conditions must both be present to justify moving a workflow to a lower model tier? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Current tier cost is above the budget AND quality testing confirms the lower tier meets the required bar
options.B: Current tier is Opus AND the workflow has been running for more than one month
options.C: Current tier output meets requirements AND a controlled test confirms the lower tier matches that quality
options.D: Response latency is above the user tolerance threshold AND the task involves document summarisation
options.E: Per-call cost exceeds a target threshold AND the prompt has been iterated fewer than three times

items.question: Which TWO of the following correctly describe how symptom-to-cause mapping differs in *long conversation threads* compared to fresh single-turn prompts? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Format failures in long threads are always caused by context window pressure rather than missing format specifications
options.B: A symptom that appears mid-thread, after earlier turns were successful, shifts the diagnosis toward context accumulation rather than a prompt gap
options.C: Instruction absence cannot cause failures in long threads because instructions were established at the start
options.D: Refusals in long threads can sometimes be caused by the accumulated context shifting the apparent nature of the conversation, rather than by a missing professional context in the current prompt
options.E: All symptoms in long threads require a fresh-chat test as the definitive first diagnostic step before any other diagnosis
